context: The Active Prompt page currently has a 2-second polling mechanism (refreshActivePromptStatuses) that updates workflow status flags and execution mode buttons. The prompt requests extending this mechanism to also update file view button states (Questionnaire, Analysis, Plan, Implementation, Modifications) in real-time. Several implementation details need clarification to ensure the extension is reliable and doesn't introduce side effects.

questions.question-text: Should the file button state updates rely solely on registry flags, or should they also verify actual file existence on disk?

options.label: Only use registry flags (questionnaire-generated, plan-generated, etc.)
options.pros: Faster execution, no additional API calls, consistent with current refreshActivePromptStatuses implementation, registry flags are the source of truth per framework design
options.cons: If files are manually deleted outside the UI, buttons might enable for non-existent files until registry is updated

options.label: Use registry flags but add file existence checks via API calls
options.pros: More robust, catches edge cases where files are deleted manually, ensures buttons only enable when files actually exist
options.cons: Requires additional API calls every 2 seconds (5 file checks per poll), potential performance impact, adds complexity and latency

options.label: Hybrid: use registry flags and add local caching of file existence results
options.pros: Better performance than option B, reduces API calls while maintaining some file existence validation
options.cons: More complex implementation, cache invalidation logic needed, may still show stale state briefly

questions.recommendation-rationale: The framework is designed with registry flags as the source of truth for workflow state. The existing updateFileButtonStates function already relies solely on registry flags, and the current refresh mechanism follows the same pattern. Consistency with existing design principles is important, and the framework provides proper scripts to update registry flags when files are created or deleted.

questions.question-text: Should the delete buttons for execution mode files (Questionnaire, Analysis, Plan) also be updated in real-time?

options.label: Yes, update delete button states in the refresh
options.pros: Complete consistency - all file-related buttons stay in sync with registry state, matches user expectation of real-time updates
options.cons: Slightly more DOM updates every 2 seconds, though minimal performance impact

options.label: No, keep delete buttons updating only on page load
options.pros: Minimal scope change, less DOM manipulation, delete actions are less frequent so real-time updates less critical
options.cons: Inconsistent UX - file view buttons update in real-time but delete buttons don't, may confuse users

questions.recommendation-rationale: For consistency and a complete real-time experience, delete buttons should update alongside view buttons. The performance impact is negligible (3 additional button state updates every 2 seconds), and having inconsistent update behavior would be confusing. The existing updateFileButtonStates function already handles delete buttons, so calling it achieves both objectives with minimal code.

questions.question-text: Should the refresh mechanism continue to use the existing updateFileButtonStates function, or create a new lightweight version?

options.label: Reuse existing updateFileButtonStates function
options.pros: DRY principle, consistent logic between page load and refresh, easier maintenance, all button states updated in one call
options.cons: Updates more buttons than might be strictly necessary (includes Add Modification button), slightly less targeted

options.label: Create a new minimal function updating only file view and delete buttons
options.pros: More targeted, only updates exactly what the prompt requests, slightly better performance
options.cons: Code duplication, two places to maintain button state logic, risk of divergence between initial load and refresh behavior

questions.recommendation-rationale: Reusing the existing updateFileButtonStates function follows the DRY principle and ensures consistent behavior between page load and background refresh. The function is already well-tested and handles all button state logic correctly. The minimal performance difference is not significant enough to justify code duplication and the maintenance burden of keeping two implementations in sync.
